title: Cascade Robotics Incident Review - Firmware Update Bricked Test Units

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Let's go through what happened with the firmware update that bricked two test units yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Mei Lin Chao
transcript.text: The update included a bootloader change. On two of our five test units, the update process lost power partway through - a loose battery connector - and because the new bootloader doesn't have a fallback partition, those two units are now unresponsive.

transcript.speaker: Gustavo Ferreira
transcript.text: That's on me - I removed the dual-partition fallback in this update to save flash space, without fully considering what happens if power is lost mid-flash. That was a mistake.

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Can the two bricked units be recovered?

transcript.speaker: Gustavo Ferreira
transcript.text: Only with a hardware JTAG connection, not over the air. I can recover them in the lab, it'll take about half a day for both.

transcript.speaker: Mei Lin Chao
transcript.text: I'll also get the loose battery connector issue looked at separately - that's a hardware assembly problem independent of the firmware bug, and it's concerning on its own.

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Agreed, two separate problems. What's the fix so this can't happen again?

transcript.speaker: Gustavo Ferreira
transcript.text: Bring back the dual-partition fallback so a failed flash always has a known-good partition to boot from. That costs some flash space, but bricking a unit is much worse. I'll restore that this week.

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Agreed, that's not a tradeoff we should make lightly again. Let's make it a rule - no bootloader changes ship without a fallback partition, full stop.

transcript.speaker: Mei Lin Chao
transcript.text: I'll add a checklist item for firmware releases to confirm fallback partition is present.

transcript.speaker: Gustavo Ferreira
transcript.text: And I'll add a brownout test to our release process - simulate power loss at several points during flashing to see how the unit recovers.

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Good. One open question I don't have an answer to - how many units in the field, if any, could be affected by this same update? Do we know how many customers already received it?

transcript.speaker: Mei Lin Chao
transcript.text: I need to check with ops on the rollout list - I don't have that number in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Noah Bergström
transcript.text: Let's get that answer before end of day given the severity.

transcript.speaker: Mei Lin Chao
transcript.text: Understood, I'll find out and report back today.

summary_key_points: Removing the dual-partition fallback to save flash space caused two test units to brick when power was lost mid-update
The two bricked units can be recovered in the lab with a JTAG connection, about half a day
The dual-partition fallback will be restored, and a rule is being set that no bootloader change ships without one
It's unclear how many field units, if any, already received the risky update

action_items.task: Recover the two bricked test units using a JTAG connection
Restore the dual-partition bootloader fallback this week
Add a brownout test simulating power loss during flashing to the release process
Add a release checklist item confirming the fallback partition is present
Find out how many field units already received the risky firmware update and report back today

decisions: No bootloader change ships without a dual-partition fallback, going forward
open_questions: How many units in the field, if any, already received the update that caused the bricking?
